children: stock dropped 7.4% in Wednesday morning trading after the payroll processing and human resources management firm reaffirmed its full-year earnings and revenue guidance even as its fiscal Q1 earnings topped the Wall Street consensus.
Total expenses in Q1 came in higher than the average Wall Street estimate, contributing to a miss in adjusted EBITDA.

for adjusted EPS growth of 7%-9% and revenue growth of 5%-6%. Meanwhile, it boosted its outlook for PEO and insurance revenue growth to 7%-8% from its prior forecast of 6%-7% and increased its guidance for interest on funds held for clients to $200M-$210M from $195M-$205M previously.
The full-year guidance implies FY2027 adjusted EPS of $5.90-$6.01 (midpoint of $5.96 in line with consensus) and revenue of $6.84B-$6.90B (midpoint of $6.87B in line with consensus).
Fiscal Q1 2027 adjusted EPS of $1.34, beating the average analyst estimate of $1.32, rose from $1.32 in Q4 2026 and $1.22 in Q1 2026.
Revenue for the quarter ended Aug. 31, 2026, was $1.63B, in line with the consensus and up 6% Y/Y, slowing from 12% Y/Y growth in Q4.
Total expenses of $1.01B, exceeding the Visible Alpha consensus of $996.3M, edged up from $1.00B in the prior quarter and grew from $998.1M a year ago.
Adjusted EBITDA of $738.3M, trailing the $740.1M S&P CapIQ consensus, increased from $729.7M in Q4 and $680.0M in Q1 2026.

Q1 management solutions revenue of $1.21B rose 4% Y/Y, slowing from 14% Y/Y growth in Q4. PEO and insurance solution revenue of $367.6M grew 12% Y/Y vs. +9% in the prior quarter. Interest on funds held for clients was $49.8M, up 5% Y/Y vs. +15% in Q4 2026.

title: Paychex stock slumps after Q1 earnings beat; earnings, revenue guidance unchanged
